title: Path traversal in a document portal
summary: A tiny document portal serves files from one folder. Show that it can be tricked into serving a file from outside that folder, then fix the code without breaking the portal.
instructions: Open the portal (the Lab app tab, or `wget -qO- http://localhost:8080/` in the terminal) and look at how documents are requested.
The portal's code is in /lab/app/server.py. Read `read_document` and ask what happens to the `name` you send.
The portal must only serve files inside /lab/docs. This lab hides a per-lab secret in a file *outside* that folder. Find a request that makes the portal return it.
Submit that request path for verification. The check replays it against the running portal and looks for this lab's secret in the answer.
Now fix the code in /lab/app/server.py, keeping legitimate documents (including ones in sub-folders) working. Restart the portal with `sh /opt/lab/restart.sh`, then verify the fix.
Everything here is disposable: use Reset lab for a fresh copy of the vulnerable portal at any time.
safety_notes: This lab is an intentionally vulnerable toy application running in a sealed container with no network access.
Do not use these techniques against systems you do not own or have written permission to test.
